name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowC
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_BuildMemberRowC(BattleActionSequence* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Third copy of the battle member-row builder (0x003C3118 / 0x003C36AC): same self+0x2EAB/0x2EC1 slot arithmetic, Text_BuildRowForMember call and paired-slot attach call. The readable body is a register-starved decode, so only the callee set is trustworthy.
evidence: The callee set still matches the confirmed builder 0x003C3118 (Text_BuildRowForMember plus Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ and maybe_Ui_Row_AttachPairedSlots), and its sibling 0x003C36AC is also still a maybe_ entry in R3_053. The body contains unaff_r5/unaff_r7 and lost arguments, so no further confidence is justified.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_Member_ApplyRowStyle
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_Member_ApplyRowStyle(BattleUiMember* self, u32 value, u32 flags)
summary: Battle member-widget vtable slot: resolves the row object through virtual +0x48 and a record through virtual +0x150, then applies the row style to self+0x49F using the member byte at +0x137A and the two incoming values.
evidence: The only named callee is the row-style applier at 0x00488638 (called with the style object, self+0x49F, the row object, the value, the per-member byte and the flags), and the body has no animation/play call at all, so the previous PlayNamedAnim reading claimed an operation that is not there. The member-widget prefix is supported by the sibling slots 0x003CB4EC/0x003CB6FC/0x003CCD90, which are named member sound slots.

name: Script_LookupIntTableValueD
signature: bool Script_LookupIntTableValueD(ScriptContext* self, u32 key, int* out)
summary: Context-table variant of the script integer lookup: calls Script_GetIntTable3 on *(self+4)+0x14, writes the found value to *out and returns whether a non-zero value was found.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x003D1B2C loads the two arguments from the incoming stack at +8, confirming that the in_stack_00000000/4 words in the damaged C are the real key and out parameters; it then calls the confident Script_GetIntTable3 and returns 1 exactly when the result is non-zero. Its C and E siblings (0x003D1AB8 / 0x003D1C50) already carry the same lookup name at 0.50.

name: Ui_Widget_SetSubPanesVisible
summary: Sets the widget sub-node at +0x4C to the incoming flag and the sub-node at +0xE8 to its complement through Gfx_Node_SetVisible; the battle enemy-list row selection uses it to swap the two popup panes.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x003D26CC is two Gfx_Node_SetVisible calls (0x0029126C): +0x4C <- r1 and +0xE8 <- !r1, and the sole caller Ui_BattleEnemyListWindow_OnRowSelected passes the popup's active flag as r1. The plural fixes the old one-node wording; the previous decompilation showed only the first call because the second is a tail branch.

name: Field_Gimmick_InitComponentE
summary: Fifth member of the field-gimmick component-init family: constructs the sub-object at +0x210 and stores its address in the component pointer at +0x12C.
evidence: Exactly the two-instruction shape of the already-named gimmick component inits A/B/C/D (sub-object constructor followed by a store into the owning gimmick), and its callers are the named Field_Gimmick_SendEventForIdRange and Field_Gimmick_CreateCompositeA. The old Ui_DungeonWindow name had no UI caller and no handler table.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_RegisterCallback
summary: If the actor has a model and that model accepts the callback block at 0x003D6048, forwards the block to the actor's virtual +0x84; otherwise does nothing.
evidence: The guard callee is still only the maybe_ Model_HasCommandByName (0x00633D6C), and both the callback block 0x003D6048 and the actor vtable slot +0x84 are unnamed. No caller or vtable slot identifies the registration event, so the name stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_FindEntry
summary: Walks a chain of 0xC-byte entries (next index at +4) comparing each entry's key word and returns the matching entry, or null at the end of the chain.
evidence: The readable body is still a misdecode: the list base arrives in unaff_r9, the key in unaff_r5 and the loop condition is in_ZR, so even the comparison targets cannot be re-read. Only the 0xC stride and the adjacent Ui_DiveForm_PopPane/PushPane calls link it to the dive form.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateSoundTimer
summary: Model timer: plays SE id 7 while bit 0 of f_288 is set, decrements f_370, and once the countdown reaches zero with f_28C set plays SE id 5 and reloads the timer with 8 frames.
evidence: The only callee is the confident Sound_Emitter_PlaySe (0x00366B38), called with ids 7 and 5; nothing in the body touches a face, eye or blink state, so the previous UpdateBlink reading described the wrong subsystem. The model class and the timer's trigger condition are still inferred from field offsets only.

name: Field_Actor_SuspendB
summary: Suspends the actor: cancels the current action through virtual +0x54(4), releases the animation controller when f_201 is set, updates the motion pose and clears f_201.
evidence: Instruction-for-instruction identical to the named Field_Actor_Suspend (0x003E7150) after normalising branch targets: same ldr [r0,#0x204] guard, same vtable +0x54 with constant 4, same func_002D12E4(f_b8), same Field_Actor_UpdateMotionPose and f_201=0. It is a template copy of the same suspend body at a second address.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_OnActionEvent
summary: Makes the actor visible, selects list entry 3 with flag 1 on its scene object and asks the action object at f_204 to finish (virtual +0x58 with 4).
evidence: Field_SceneObject_ForceVisible (0x005F4E48) and the ShowAndSelectEntry tail 0x005E74A0 are named, so the sequence is clear, but no caller or vtable slot identifies the event that invokes it; the event name therefore stays a maybe_.

name: Field_HitBox_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the integer hit/collision box object: runs the base constructor, installs vtable 0x0076B63C and clears the bounds words at +0x24..+0x30.
evidence: Both partners are now confident: Field_HitBox_Setup (0x003EA25C) and Field_HitBox_SetupFloat (0x003EA420). Model_RebuildPartListB builds exactly this 0x34-byte object and immediately runs Setup on it, and the 0x3C-byte twin (0x003EA5F0) is the float constructor.

name: Field_HitBox_CtorFloat
summary: Constructor of the float hit/collision box: base constructor, vtable 0x0076B65C, and copies the shared six-float default extents at 0x007E71EC into +0x24..+0x38.
evidence: Model_RebuildPartListA allocates 0x3C bytes, calls this constructor and immediately runs the confident Field_HitBox_SetupFloat (0x003EA420) on the result; its integer twin 0x003EA3E0 is the non-float variant with the 0x34-byte object size.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_SetRowValueDigits
summary: Fills the seven smith-menu row cells: for each of seven rows it decomposes the row's item value into decimal digits, writes them into the three sub-nodes at +0x2EC/+0x33C/+0x38C and toggles each node's visibility for the >=10 and >=100 thresholds.
evidence: The 788-byte body is not a marker toggle: the disassembly shows a seven-iteration loop with repeated division-by-10 digit extraction and a call into 0x004CF44C per digit, plus three Gfx_Node_SetVisible calls per row (thresholds 10 and 100). Only the caller Ui_SmithMenu_DetailOpen names the menu, so the class stays inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_SevenSlotRow_SetSlotIcons
summary: Stores the mode byte, fills the seven slot bytes with 0xFF placeholders or 0..6, then writes one Ui_TextLayer_SetText value per cell (slot id | row<<16), using the alternate value for slot 1 while the menu is open.
evidence: The per-cell setter is the named Ui_TextLayer_SetText (0x001D.. path), which confirms the seven-cell write and the mode-dependent fill. Whether the values are icons or text ids is still not decidable, so the icon wording stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_DelegateIfAttached
summary: Looks the command name up on the scene node's model (self->f_160->f_11c); when found it forwards (self, command) to 0x005F6000, otherwise returns 1.
evidence: Actor_FindCommandByName (0x00641628) is a table search taking (actor, name), which explains why r1 is forwarded unchanged to both callees, but the delegate 0x005F6000 and the table 0x0076BDB8 are still unnamed and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Field_Billboard_SyncTransformFromSource
summary: Updates the billboard's effect-part transform and copies the source object's +0x88 transform word back into the billboard.
evidence: Both callers are the named billboard builders Field_Actor_CreateBillboard (0x00182F0C) and Model_CreateBillboardPart (0x002306B8), and the callee is the confident Gfx_EffectPart_UpdateTransform (0x005F79E0); the +0x174 source field is the same one that function documents, so this is a billboard-part sync, not a generic scene-node operation.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncTaskChain
summary: Attaches or detaches the object's task chain (self+0x2C8) to match the actor state byte f_312 (state 7 uses the detach helper 0x002337CC, other states the attach helper Actor_CreateTaskChainB) and returns whether it changed anything.
evidence: The disassembly confirms the actor state is only read, never written (the older SwapActorState reading was inverted), and the only writes go to &self->f_2c8. The two branch helpers 0x002337CC and Actor_CreateTaskChainB still lack confident names, so what the chain controls remains inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Action_ApplyAnimResource
summary: Lazily builds a 0xA24-byte shared animation-resource buffer, resolves its sub-block with 0x0063D6B8(buf,4) and pushes the block at +0x38 into the actor through virtual +0x84 (twice, with +0x88 between) so the animation restarts.
evidence: Vtable 0x0076DFA0's other named slots are Field_Action_UpdateAnim and Field_Action_UpdateNutState, so the class prefix is Field_Action rather than Field_ActorAction. The resource helper 0x0063D6B8 and the actor virtuals +0x84/+0x88 are still unnamed, so what exactly is applied stays inferred.

name: Ui_Window_PushCallback
summary: Pushes a 0x14-byte callback frame onto the window's callback stack at +0x1C68, forwards the copied frame to the currently installed callback when one exists, and finishes with 0x0036B510.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_ListWindow_DispatchInput, so the previous Ui_TalkWindow class label was wrong; the record copy matches the sibling push at 0x0041B280 and the local frame installs vtable 0x00766058 before calling the parent callback.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_DispatchFrame
summary: Calls the object's own virtual frame handler at slot +0x64 only while Field_Marker_IsAnyVisible() is true; otherwise does nothing.
evidence: The gate 0x0047B470 is the named (0.50) marker-visibility scan and the vtable 0x0076EA68 has no confident sibling at +0x64, so both the frame and the marker halves remain unproven; no caller reaches it directly.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubObject_AddEntry
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SubObject_AddEntry(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u16 id)
summary: Forwards all incoming arguments to Container_AddUniqueIdEntry on the container sub-object at self+0x14 (same operand registers plus the stack word), i.e. it is the class's add-entry thunk rather than a release.
evidence: The asm is exactly add r0,#0x14, forward r1-r3 and the stack argument, tail-call Container_AddUniqueIdEntry (0x0047E7A8). That callee is the confident add-if-absent helper, so the previous Release name contradicted the operation.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutAnim_SetTarget
summary: Twelve-byte tail-branch into Anim_Tween_SetTarget (0x006E6F04); all arguments stay in registers, so neither the target nor the easing can be read.
evidence: There is no caller and the readable body has no argument list; the only fact is the tail target, which is already named. The wrapper's own role therefore stays a maybe_, and the disassembly in this region is misaligned (Thumb/ARM mixed), so no argument evidence can be recovered.

name: Ui_DiveManager_BindContext
summary: Binds the shared context/owner into the dive manager: stores it at f_2984/f_9BC, points f_BEC at context+0x494 and rebinds the update callback and the eight-row list at f_4B8/f_728.
evidence: The sole caller is the named Ui_DiveManager_Ctor (0x0032C4BC) and the function is a pure field-store plus rebind sequence; the rebind targets Ui_BindUpdateCallback and Ui_EightRowList_FillRowsFrom are both named.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_FinishLoadForPanel
summary: Stores the mode byte at panel+0x29D, gets the UI root singleton through an out-parameter and runs Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad on it, finishing the pending icon load for this panel.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x004662D4 reads only r1 (the mode) and writes r0=sp as the out-parameter for Ui_GetRootSingleton; the old id/self parameters were Ghidra fiction. The operation is the finish stage, not a load start, so 'LoadForPanel' was one stage off.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectKind30_Ctor
summary: Constructor for the object factory's kind-30 class: runs the shared Ui_ScreenObject_CtorBase, installs the class descriptor and initialises the two fields at +0x17FC (-1) and +0x1800 (0).
evidence: The sole caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind30, which allocates the 0x1804-byte 3D/2D variants, matching the project convention of naming factory-only constructors by kind (cf. Field_ObjectKind15_Ctor / Field_ObjectKind16_Ctor). The installed descriptor is still only the low-confidence maybe_g_fieldPartyObjectClassDesc.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_StopActorIfIdle
summary: When the model/attachment root has no pending update (Model_Attach_ShouldUpdateRoot == 0), sends the scene object's select-entry command (entry 0, flag 1) at 0x005E7848.
evidence: Both callees are named, but 0x005E7848 is only a tail entry into the keyed-list select helper (it branches to 0x002A891C with entry 0), so 'stop the idle actor' remains an interpretation of 'select entry 0'. No caller or vtable slot names the owning widget.

name: maybe_Camera_AnimTrackCtor_vt7731C8
summary: Derived-class constructor: runs the base constructor 0x004D7124 (which installs vtable 0x00779E64) and overwrites the vtable with 0x007731C8.
evidence: The disassembly is base-constructor plus a single vtable store at [r0]; callers are Battle_CameraRangeBlend_Update and maybe_Field_SetEncounterParams. Vtable 0x007731C8 and the base class at 0x004D7124 are unnamed, so the camera-track class label stays a guess.

name: Ui_List_GetSelectionIndex
summary: Returns the current selection index of the list entry at self+0x38 (sign-extended u16 at +0xC), or -1 when the list model's active bit is clear.
evidence: The disassembly shows the gate 0x0062AF84 testing bit 0 of [model+8]+0x44 and the getter then returning the signed halfword at [model+0xC]; both call sites compare the result against entry indices (for example 4), which fits a selection index rather than a count.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcAttackMultiplier_Prologue
summary: Not a callable function: the 24 bytes are only the ARM prologue (save r4/r5/r7, vpush d8-d10, reserve 0x1C bytes) that falls through into the real body at 0x0048C4A8, maybe_Battle_CalcAttackMultiplier_Body.
evidence: The symbol ends exactly at 0x0048C4A8, where the split body begins; the prologue sets r1=8 and keeps r0 in r4 for the body's first call 0x00639954. The previous Text_LayoutStub name came from Ghidra failing on the truncated decode (coprocessor_load/halt_baddata), so it is battle maths, not text layout.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ReleaseEffectBindings
summary: Releases the scene object's effect bindings: calls Field_SceneObject_ReleaseEffectSlots when f_41 is set, notifies the field manager (work+8->+0x54, 0x001C9110) for the id at f_26C, then releases the packed effect handle at f_2FC through the 0x007B4D68 table.
evidence: The readable C is a bad-data fragment, but the disassembly at 0x004C9BCC shows pure release calls: 0x00336938 Field_SceneObject_ReleaseEffectSlots, 0x001C9110, and 0x0035FC84 Effect_ReleaseHandle with the handle from f_2FC. There is no mesh/loading call, so BeginMeshLoad was the wrong direction.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_RegisterCallback
summary: Registers the window with its owner's callback list: copies the listener triple from the global 0x0072B220 into self+0x8F4..+0x908, links owner+0x2C into that node and stores the owner at self+0x8EC.
evidence: Called from Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor and the link helper 0x001235A4 is the shared intrusive-list link, but the global listener table 0x0072B220 and the exact callback role are unnamed, so the registration reading stays tentative.

name: Ui_3DBackground_DeletingDtorB
summary: Second deleting-destructor thunk of the 3D background window: runs Ui_3DBackground_DtorBody and frees the object.
evidence: Byte-identical to the already-named Ui_3DBackground_DeletingDtor (0x00463B24): the same DtorBody (0x00463B34) followed by the operator-delete tail 0x0010F6CC. It is a second vtable instance of the same destructor, not a different class.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_HideTarget
summary: When the scene-node system is active, hides/resets the target pane with the hide slots +0x58 and +0x40 (command 4); this is exactly the hide branch of Ui_MessagePanel_HideOrShowByFlag.
evidence: The sibling 0x004DD390 is the named two-way HideOrShowByFlag and this body contains only its hide pair (vtable +0x58 then +0x40 with constant 4). Nothing reads a mode or reacts to a change event, so OnModeChange described an event that is not in the code.

name: maybe_Battle_AnimWindow_DtorWithVtable
summary: Deleting-destructor helper of the battle animation-window family: stores the vtable passed in r1 at +0 and its secondary table at +0x220, runs Battle_AnimWindow_ReleaseHandles and frees the object.
evidence: The disassembly shows the store of the incoming vtable (and vtable+0xB8 into +0x220), then 0x002F19AC Battle_AnimWindow_ReleaseHandles and the operator-delete tail 0x0010F6CC. The destructor body is the battle anim-window one, not Ui3D_Panel, and the function takes the vtable explicitly rather than loading a literal.

name: Battle_AnimWindow_DeleteB
summary: Third deleting-destructor thunk of the battle animation window: releases the animation handles and frees the object.
evidence: Byte-identical to the named Battle_AnimWindow_Delete (0x0059F844) and Battle_AnimWindow_Dtor (0x002F199C): Battle_AnimWindow_ReleaseHandles followed by the operator-delete tail 0x0010F6CC. It is another vtable's slot 0, not a unit-specific 'release anim window'.

name: maybe_Anim_Clip_UpdateThunk
summary: Twelve-byte thunk that calls Anim_Clip_Update(self) and always returns 0.
evidence: The disassembly is bl 0x0029E59C, mov r0,#0, pop {r4,pc}; there is no direction or 'forward' argument, and the constant zero return is the only thing distinguishing it from the shared updater, so UpdateForward was over-specific.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionModel_CommitAttachNodes
summary: Commits the two model node references at +0x40 and +0x48 through Model_Equip_CommitNodeChanges; does nothing when the action has no model (self->f_28->f_224).
evidence: The callee is the confident Model_Equip_CommitNodeChanges (0x0040A8C4) and the two offsets are the model-equip node blocks it expects, but no caller or vtable slot names the owning battle-action class, so the prefix stays maybe_.

name: Gfx_Texture_SwizzleAndConvert
signature: unsigned int Gfx_Texture_SwizzleAndConvert(void* dst, int dstSize, int* src, int* srcSize, int* arg5, int* arg6)
summary: Converts and re-tiles a texture block between linear and 8x8-tiled layout for format ids 0x64..0x6F, swapping channels per RGBA/RGB/LA variant and using a staging buffer when source and destination overlap.
evidence: The inner loop computes ((y>>3)*(width>>3)+(x>>3))*0x40 plus the in-tile offset (the standard 8x8 GX/PICA swizzle) and the format switch selects the channel order for 32/24/16/4-bit layouts. The only caller, Gfx_TryConvertBuffer (0x00525494), is named and the 1236-byte body is intact.

name: maybe_Svc_Ipc_Send0007
summary: Sends IPC header 0x00070040 with one normal parameter on the session stored at 0x007B00E8 and returns the reply parameter (or the raw result on error).
evidence: The header and session literals are certain and the asm is a clean mrc/svc 0x32 wrapper, but 0x007B00E8 has no data symbol and the recorded callers are literal-pool artefacts (no bl site exists in asm/text), so the service is still unknown.

name: maybe_Err_WaitForIpcIdleOrFatal
summary: Retries Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle(0) while it reports a negative non-fatal result, sleeping 10 ms on 0xE0A0CC08 and stopping on success or on the err:f sentinel 0xC8A0CFFC.
evidence: The loop constants are the err:f family values (FACTS.md: 0xC8A0CFFC) and the callee is the named Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle, so this waits rather than checking a returned value; the previous '1 ms' wording was wrong (0x00989680 ns = 10 ms).

name: Gfx_BuildVertexFormatDescriptor
summary: Builds the PICA200 vertex-attribute block: attribute-buffer headers at 0x0201/0x0203, a 0x98-byte cleared region, twelve FIXEDATTRIB_INDEX entries (register 0x0232, index 0..11) and the chained sub-descriptors, returning the final descriptor.
evidence: The command words write registers 0x0201/0x0203 and 0x0232 with mask 0x3F - the PICA200 vertex-attribute command set listed in FACTS.md - and there are exactly 12 attribute entries. The four builder helpers and 15 draw-path callers are named.

name: Svc_Cecd_OpenRawWithRetry
signature: void Svc_Cecd_OpenRawWithRetry(u32 self, u32 id, u32 size, void* buffer, u32 a5, u32 a6, u32 a7, u32 a8)
summary: Opens a raw CECD file through Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile and, on 0xC8A10BF0 'not started', starts the service, sets the retry byte at 0x007AE9E6 and retries the open once.
evidence: The callee is the named Cecd command-0x03 open wrapper (0x0050C328), so the previous Ui_IconCache prefix was wrong. The disassembly shows r0 is a discarded vtable self and the seven following register/stack values are forwarded unchanged.

name: Svc_Cecd_ReadRawWithRetry
signature: void Svc_Cecd_ReadRawWithRetry(u32 self, u32 id, u32 size, u32 destination, u32 a5, u32 a6, u32 a7, u32 a8)
summary: Reads a raw CECD file through Svc_Cecd_ReadRawFile and retries once after starting the service when it returns 0xC8A10BF0.
evidence: The callee is the named command-0x07 raw-read wrapper (0x0050C55C). The disassembly matches the 0x0050BF64 dispatch read retry one-for-one but calls ReadRawFile instead of ReadDispatch, so the distinct Raw name is required (ReadWithRetry already belongs to 0x0050BF64).

name: maybe_Svc_Cecd_Cmd0009WithRetry
signature: void maybe_Svc_Cecd_Cmd0009WithRetry(u32 self, u32 value, u32 buffer, int size, u32 flags)
summary: Retry wrapper for CECD command 0x0009: dispatches through 0x0050D050, and on 0xC8A10BF0 starts the service, sets the retry byte and dispatches once more.
evidence: The disassembly at 0x0050D050 shows the callee is the Cmd0009/Cmd0009B session dispatcher (header 0x000900C2 with value, size, flags and buffer), not the delete dispatcher. CECD delete is command 0x11 (Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawFile) and 0x0A (DeleteDispatch), so the old DeleteWithRetry wording was not supported by the command number.

name: maybe_Svc_Cfg_GetRegionInfo
summary: Sends command 0x0003 with one normal parameter on the cfg session at 0x007AF0F8 and copies the 64-bit reply into outPair.
evidence: The session and command shape are certain, but no caller and no data symbol name 0x007AF0F8; the only anchor is that the sibling 0x0050D9BC uses the same session for the system-language query, so 'region' remains a guess.

name: maybe_Svc_Ipc_Send0001
summary: Sends IPC header 0x00010042 with one normal parameter and a 0x20-byte descriptor on the session at 0x007B00E8, returning the reply parameter or the raw error.
evidence: The header/descriptor literals and the svc 0x32 sequence are certain, but 0x007B00E8 is unnamed and the recorded callers come from literal-pool misdecodes (there is no bl site), so the service stays unidentified.

name: maybe_Svc_Ipc_Send0002
summary: Sends IPC request 0x00020002 with a 0x20-byte translate descriptor and no normal parameter on the session at 0x007B00E8, returning the reply parameter or the raw error.
evidence: The literal header and the 0x20 descriptor size are exact, but the session remains unnamed and the only 'callers' are the same literal-pool artefacts as its two siblings, so the command identity is unproven.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSprite
signature: u32* maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSprite(u32 self, u32* out, void* particle, float* colour, int flag, int flag2, int flag3)
summary: Emits one particle sprite's draw record: scales the template colour by the frame colour, writes the 0x28-word PICA vertex/UV/colour block and returns the advanced write pointer.
evidence: The body appends the command words 0x8000004C/0x000F02C0/0x023F02C1 and returns the advanced pointer, so it emits rather than updating stored state; the four calls per particle from maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListI confirm the emit role.

name: maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSpriteB
signature: u32* maybe_Fx_EmitParticleSpriteB(u32 self, u32* out, void* particle, float* colour, int flag, int flag2, int flag3)
summary: Second particle-sprite emit path: same 0x28-word draw record, but the UV/position terms come from the emitter template at +0xDC instead of the keyframe copy.
evidence: Same field set and command words as 0x0052943C with the template base, so it is a variant emitter rather than a new operation; its caller maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListJ keeps both sides below 0.5.

name: maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleTrail
signature: void maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleTrail(int self, float* particle, int update)
summary: Maintains a particle's 0x58-byte-stride trail history: smooths with 0.7, advances the ring write indices and appends the current position/rotation segments.
evidence: The body works on the 0x584C..0x586C ring of 0x58-byte segments with the 0x3F333333 (0.7) smoothing and calls std_FastSinCos/std_Expf, which is a trail/ribbon update rather than a generic list walk. The 0x58 segment layout is still inferred from offsets and the caller is a maybe_ dispatcher.
